newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYBEANS END HIGHER ON DRIER WEATHER OUTLOOK.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYBEANS END HIGHER ON DRIER WEATHER OUTLOOK.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures surged higher on Wednesday, lifted by forecasts that suggested weekend rains would remain north of parched portions of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

"You change the weather forecast, you change the market," said Dale Durchholz, analyst with Agrivisor Services. "The whole soybean market is directly correlated to the weather right now. Any little subtle tweak in the forecast is going to move prices."
Forecasts called for showers this weekend in the U.S. Midwest but some meteorologists said coverage would be light.
Weather Services Corp senior agricultural meteorologist David Taylor said showers may be lightest in the areas where corn and soybean crops most need moisture.
WSC predicted a weekend storm system would bring 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain to the U.S. Corn Belt on Sunday or Monday with 40 to 60 percent coverage.
That scenario differed from some wetter outlooks issued earlier this week that contributed to sharp declines in new crop soybeans.
Soybean futures ended 15-1/2 to six cents per bushel higher with November up 15-1/2 at $6.50 a bushel.
Trade sources also pointed to short covering ahead of Thursday's USDA export sales data and Tuesday's USDA crop production report.

The trade expected old-crop export sales to come in at 50,000 to 125,000 tonnes but ideas varied on new-crop sales with some suggesting a figure of minus 300,000 tonnes and others leaning toward plus 300,000.
The discrepancy was tied to rumors that China had cancelled new crop purchases but the trade was unsure about the amount or timing of the cancellations.
Commercials were light buyers of the November.
Farmers Commodities Corp bought three million bushels November and sold one million, Produce Grain bought two million November and sold 1.5 million, and Cargill Inc bought one million November.
Refco Inc bought 3.5 million bushels November and sold 2.5 million and Cargill Investor Services bought two million November.
In options trade, Refco sold 200 September $7.25 calls at six cents. Options volatility in the November was pegged at 27 percent, up from Tuesday's 26 percent.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 45,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 47,485.
